name: Dedalus Labs

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: 50 active compute-hours/month ceiling (hard free-plan limit); 10 GiB storage per machine hard cap; up to 4 vCPU / 16 GiB per machine; up to 5 machines.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $20 monthly compute credit, refreshes each cycle, does not roll over (purchased credits do roll over). Configurable timeout; unlimited compute; up to 16 vCPU / 64 GiB, 20 machines.

free.notes: Startup program: up to $10,000 compute credits valid 12 months for qualifying startups.

caveats: Cloud Hypervisor-derived custom VMM; CPU/RAM charged per second while actively running, idle sleep free. This is lifecycle-active, not proven CPU-utilization billing.

Storage headline incorrectly labels $0.073 as per GiB-hour; calculator/FAQ explicitly use $0.0001/GiB-hour ($0.073 at 730h). Use FAQ and preserve conflict. Unlimited Pro storage means capacity, not free bytes.

Hobby 5 machines and 50 compute-hours/month; Pro 20 machines. Fifty concurrent requires Enterprise, whose fee and rates are unknown. Pricing footer says join waitlist: public rates do not prove instant admission.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
SSH verified 2026-09-28: skill docs say "Use dedalus ssh $MACHINE_ID for an interactive shell" (https://docs.dedaluslabs.ai/.well-known/skills/dedalus-machines/skill.md).
Lifecycle mutations are rate limited (RATE_LIMITED, scope mutating_lifecycle_routes, retry_after_ms) with no published numeric limit.
SSH sessions close after 30 idle minutes or 12 hours total; deleted machines' storage may be retained up to 30 days.

Autosleep default is 300 idle seconds ('Machines sleep after five minutes of inactivity by default'); pricing says 'Idle time is free' and billing is for active compute, but docs say compute billing stops on sleep. Whether the up-to-5-minute idle tail before autosleep is billed is not stated.

fleet.verification: Hobby says no credit card; beta organization grant required.
fleet.notes: Machine creation also requires DCS beta admission; authenticated API access alone does not prove eligibility. A BETA_ACCESS_REQUIRED response needs support to check the org grant. 50/300/1,000 are not published self-serve allowances. Machine count is a published provisioning allowance; docs and footer also advertise waitlist access.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Only the root filesystem survives sleep and wake.
snapshot_auto.note: Docs list what is lost on every sleep: 'RAM, running processes, vCPU state'. Autosleep (default 300 idle s) stops the VM; only the persistent root disk survives (that is persistent_disk, not a snapshot). Pricing FAQ mentions 'observed logical storage snapshots' but only as the storage-billing measurement method.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can create a Machine, run non-interactive commands, open a temporary Secure Shell (SSH) session, change its resources, put it to sleep, and wake it later with its root filesystem intact.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The complete public OpenAPI (https://docs.dedaluslabs.ai/dcs-openapi.json: machines, executions, SSH, artifacts, usage; ops create/update/sleep/wake/reboot/delete) and CLI command index have no snapshot/checkpoint/fork/template/image operation; CreateMachineRequest only takes vcpu, memory_mib, storage_gib, autosleep.

harness_api.quote: An execution runs one non-interactive command inside one Machine. Create returns an `execution_id`.
harness_api.note: Only a generic exec API (executions with events/output) plus SSH; no Claude Code/Codex/agent-session API. The 'agent skill' is a SKILL.md that teaches an outside coding agent to drive the CLI, not an in-sandbox harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: no network-facing surface exposed by default — machines get private IPs and don't accept inbound connections directly.
ingress_rules.note: No port exposure / preview URL feature at all, so no ingress controls to configure: machines are private-only; reach them through authenticated, temporary SSH sessions (CLI does SSH port forwards). Not 'every port public', but no public exposure option either.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM with its own guest kernel and root (custom Cloud Hypervisor fork), so nftables/iptables inside should work; not documented.

secret_proxy.note: Only mechanism to pass secrets is env vars per execution (CreateExecutionRequest.env). Dedalus Auth (DAuth, https://www.dedaluslabs.ai/blog/dedalus-auth-launch) is a separate MCP-server credential enclave product, not an outbound-request proxy for Machines.

volume_attach.quote: Persistent storage allocated to the machine, measured in gibibytes (GiB).
volume_attach.note: Only a resizable per-machine root disk (storage_gib); no volume resources in the OpenAPI or endpoint catalog.

volume_shared.quote: Persistent storage allocated to the machine, measured in gibibytes (GiB).
volume_shared.note: Storage is per machine; no shared filesystem/volume feature in API or docs (storage is 'disaggregated from compute' internally, but not shareable).

image_oci.quote: Create provisions a persistent Linux machine with the CPU, memory, storage, and autosleep policy you choose.
image_oci.note: Create params are only vcpu, memory_mib, storage_gib, autosleep (confirmed in dcs-openapi.json CreateMachineRequest); no custom image/OCI/Dockerfile parameter exists. Matches card's existing custom_image:false.

docker_inside.quote: Flexibility: Full Linux with systemd, package managers, and root access.
docker_inside.note: Not explicitly tested/documented by the provider, but the machine is a full Linux guest kernel with root and systemd (not a restricted container), so installing and running Docker/Podman is standard; no documented restriction against it.

desktop.quote: Because a computer for agents is a full Linux machine, it supports a GUI stack the same way any Linux desktop or CI runner would, with no special casing required.
desktop.note: not offered: no managed VNC/RDP/stream desktop is shipped; a GUI stack is only possible if the user installs and configures one themselves inside the generic Linux VM.

browser.quote: Driving a browser for a computer-use task requires a display server, a real Chromium process, genuine network access, and often root to install dependencies — all things a locked-down runtime typically can't provide.
browser.note: not offered: no bundled/managed browser; the docs describe this as something the user can install themselves on the generic Linux VM, not a provided feature.

computer_use.quote: An execution runs one non-interactive command inside one Machine. Create returns an `execution_id`.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only a generic non-interactive exec API and SSH exist; there is no screenshot/click computer-use API.

anti_bot.quote: Persistent Linux VMs that start in under 50ms, built for AI agents.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Dedalus Machines is a generic persistent Linux VM/compute product, not a browser-automation or scraping service; no stealth/fingerprinting feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Persistent Linux VMs that start in under 50ms, built for AI agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented anywhere in the product's docs or pricing.

egress_ip_type.quote: machines get private IPs and don't accept inbound connections directly.
egress_ip_type.note: Machines egress from Dedalus's own datacenter infrastructure; no residential/mobile/static-IP proxy product is offered, so outbound traffic is ordinary datacenter-range IP.

fork_running.quote: You can create a Machine, run non-interactive commands, open a temporary Secure Shell (SSH) session, change its resources, put it to sleep, and wake it later with its root filesystem intact.
fork_running.note: No fork/clone operation exists at all in the public OpenAPI (create/update/sleep/wake/reboot/delete only), consistent with the card's existing fork:false, so cloning a running machine is not possible.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: You can create a Machine, run non-interactive commands, open a temporary Secure Shell (SSH) session, change its resources, put it to sleep, and wake it later with its root filesystem intact.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork/clone/template operation exists; there is no memory-including clone feature. Consistent with fork:false.

wake_on_request.quote: Operations that need the machine, such as an execution or SSH session, wake it as part of the request.
wake_on_request.note: A sleeping machine automatically wakes when an execution or SSH request targets it.

live_resize.quote: Update changes one or more configured resources. Fields you leave out keep their current values.
live_resize.note: The update/PATCH endpoint changes vcpu, memory_mib, or storage_gib on an existing machine_id; docs do not state the machine must be stopped/sleeping first, so this is treated as an in-place resize rather than recreation.

agent_harnesses.quote: Dedalus Machines skill: Install with `npx skills add https://docs.dedaluslabs.ai --skill dedalus-machines`.
agent_harnesses.note: The "agent skill" is a SKILL.md teaching an external coding agent (e.g. Claude Code) how to call the Machines CLI/API; no coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) is preinstalled inside a Machine or offered as a machine template.

own_agent_api.quote: An execution runs one non-interactive command inside one Machine.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for Dedalus Machines. The API only exposes generic machine lifecycle/exec/SSH operations; there is no first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API (that is a separate, unrelated Dedalus Agents/router product, not Machines).

mcp_server.note: Dedalus Labs' GitHub org publishes many MCP *server* repos (github-mcp, browser-use-mcp, playwright-mcp, etc.), but these are third-party-style integrations for its separate Dedalus Agents/model-routing product, not an MCP server for controlling Dedalus Machines (sandboxes). No dedalus-machines-mcp / dcs-mcp repo or doc page exists.

public_ipv4.quote: no network-facing surface exposed by default — machines get private IPs and don't accept inbound connections directly.
public_ipv4.note: Machines get private IPs, not public IPv4 addresses.

inbound_https.quote: no network-facing surface exposed by default — machines get private IPs and don't accept inbound connections directly.
inbound_https.note: No inbound connections of any kind (HTTPS or otherwise); the only ways in are provider-brokered temporary SSH sessions or the executions API.

egress_allowlist.note: The published API surface has no network/egress configuration object (no allow/deny list, no no-internet mode, no security groups); egress control is not documented as a feature.

egress_http_rules.note: No method/path-level egress rule feature exists in the public API; there's no coarse egress control at all, let alone HTTP-method/path-level rules.

static_egress_ip.quote: Guest IP and MAC address (re-derived from a reassigned slot, so not stable)
static_egress_ip.note: Docs explicitly state the machine's network address is not stable across sleep/wake, and there is no documented static/dedicated egress IP product.

gpu.quote: Persistent Linux VMs that start in under 50ms, built for AI agents.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's current scope. Pricing/docs describe only vCPU + RAM + storage machines; no GPU instance type, GPU pricing, or GPU flag is documented anywhere (card's gpu_types is also empty).

windows.quote: Dedalus Labs builds Dedalus Machines: persistent Linux virtual machines that start in under 50ms.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product is explicitly Linux-only VMs.

macos.quote: Dedalus Labs builds Dedalus Machines: persistent Linux virtual machines that start in under 50ms.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product is explicitly Linux-only VMs.

arm64.note: The documented example `uname -a` output shows x86_64; no ARM/aarch64 machine option is advertised anywhere in pricing or docs.

self_host.note: Dedalus Machines is offered only as a hosted cloud API (dcs.dedaluslabs.ai); no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option is documented.

open_source.note: The CLI and client SDKs (dedalus-cli, dedalus-python, dedalus-typescript, dedalus-go, all MIT/Apache-2.0) are open source, but the core Dedalus Machines VM/hypervisor platform itself is a closed, proprietary hosted service.

max_session_h.quote: Accepts durations such as `30s`, `15m`, `2h`, raw seconds, or `never` to disable autosleep.
max_session_h.note: A running machine has no maximum-session cutoff enforced by the provider; autosleep can be disabled entirely (`never`), so a machine can run until the owner stops or deletes it. (The unrelated 30-min-idle/12h-total limit applies only to an individual SSH session, not the Machine's overall running lifetime.)

snapshot.quote: paths: /v1/machines, /v1/machines/{machine_id}, .../executions*, .../reboot, .../sleep, .../ssh, .../wake — no snapshot/checkpoint/image endpoint of any kind; CreateMachineRequest properties are only ['autosleep','memory_mib','storage_gib','vcpu']
snapshot.note: Sleep/wake only preserves the persistent root disk (persistent_disk=true), not a snapshot object; there is no filesystem-only or memory checkpoint API/CLI verb anywhere in the OpenAPI spec or llms-full.txt. Matches existing feature_evidence for snapshot_auto/snapshot_on_demand (both false).

fork.note: No 'fork', 'clone', or 'duplicate' term appears anywhere in the full docs text (llms-full.txt) or the OpenAPI endpoint/schema catalog; each machine is created individually via POST /v1/machines with only vcpu/memory_mib/storage_gib/autosleep.

custom_image.note: The machine-creation request schema has no image/OCI/docker-image field, and no 'image' or 'template' terminology appears in llms-full.txt; machines are provisioned only by resource size, not from a user-supplied image.

lang_python.quote: For a direct program call, use an array such as `["python3", "script.py", "--flag"]` without a shell.
lang_python.note: Docs use python3 directly as a first-class execution example (no apt-get/install step shown first), and the security-posture blog lists `pip install` as one of the routine things agents do on a Machine, consistent with a full Linux VM image that ships Python out of the box.

soc2.note: Dedalus Labs runs a Vanta-hosted Trust Center listing generic infrastructure/organizational/product security controls, but the only published Resource is an auditor 'Engagement Letter' (the document issued when an audit engagement begins), with no SOC 2 report, badge, or 'SOC 2' text anywhere on the page. This indicates a SOC 2 process has been engaged but not yet completed/attested.

eu_data_residency.note: The API, CLI, and machine-creation schema (vcpu, memory_mib, storage_gib, autosleep) have no region/location parameter anywhere in the OpenAPI spec, docs, or pricing page; the company is headquartered and its infra described only in San Francisco, CA, with no second region or EU presence advertised.
